title: Closed proper base change on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, and an admissible commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$: a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with exactly the discrete or induced $\ell$-adic topological condensed-ring convention of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the finite constant scalar-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, $q:Y\to S$ proper and $f:X\to Y$ proper, and $c:C\hookrightarrow Y$ a closed immersion whose complementary open immersion is quasi-compact [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Form $X_C=X\times_Y C$, with projections $a:X_C\to X$ and $f_C:X_C\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $L\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$ the canonical ambient exchange map [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]
$$c^*Rf_*L\longrightarrow R(f_C)_*a^*L$$
is an isomorphism in $D_C$. Pullback means the exact module inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient rings. There is no field, characteristic, Noetherian, finite-dimensional-base, or density hypothesis.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism: proper base change along the closed complement, on the bounded constructible finite-Tor generator. Agent formulation in the qcqs scope of det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle; not an attribution of this full coefficient/ambient-category statement to a narrower source theorem.

proof.text: Properness over the qcqs scheme $S$ makes $Y$ and $X$ qcqs. The closed subschemes $C$ and $X_C$ are qcqs, and $f_C$ is proper. The complement condition says that $c$ and its pullback $a$ are constructible closed immersions. A quasi-compact open of $X$ meets the closed $X_C$ in a quasi-compact open, so preimages of constructible strata are constructible. Pullback takes each finite constant scalar presentation $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ to the identical presentation on the pulled-back cover by the scalar/pullback comparison. If $L$ has Tor amplitude in $[p,r]$ and $N$ is a $\Lambda_{X_C}$-module, the closed counit $a^*a_*N\cong N$ and the pullback/tensor comparison give $a^*L\otimes^{\mathbf L}N\cong a^*(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_*N)$, whose cohomology lies in $[p,r]$ since $a^*$ is exact. Thus $a^*$ preserves the bounded constructible finite-Tor input classes used below. In the finite discrete coefficient case, the exact coefficient equivalence and qcqs constructible comparison give an étale-origin witness for $L$. The finite-level proper-base-change theorem gives the required isomorphism. The internal/section functor comparisons transport to the derived categories through their universal derived comparisons; the unit--square--counit formula transports to that same formula, so this proves invertibility of the actual ambient exchange, not merely an isomorphism of its endpoints.

proof.text: Let now $A=\mathcal O_F$, including $\mathbf Z_\ell$, and $L\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,A)$. The finite-model adic criterion gives completeness of $L$ and bounded classical finite reductions. The integral ambient-tower comparison applies to the qcqs morphism $f$, so $Rf_*L$ is complete. Closed inverse image is exact and preserves countable products. Applying it to the strict Roos complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T:\prod L_n\to\prod L_n)[-1]$ preserves this complex and its zero-second-coordinate augmentation. Exact inverse image also takes the two-term quotient resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\pi^n}A]$ to that same resolution. Therefore $c^*Rf_*L$ is complete, and the same argument with $a$ proves completeness of $a^*L$. Applying the ambient-tower comparison to $f_C$ proves completeness of $R(f_C)_*a^*L$. These are ordinary direct images throughout; none is replaced by a completed direct image.

source.place: Corollary 6.1.5, Lemma 6.5.9 and Remark 6.5.10; strict augmentation rather than an unspecified inverse-limit isomorphism

proof.text: Reduce the integral ambient exchange modulo $\pi$. The integral quotient-exchange comparison identifies this specific reduced map, through its invertible pull/reduction and quotient direct-image comparisons, with the finite-coefficient ambient exchange for $L_1$. By the adic criterion $L_1$ has a bounded-below étale-origin witness, so finite-level proper base change makes this map invertible. Both integral endpoints are complete by step 2. Derived Nakayama, transported through the exact internal/section equivalences with their quotient comparisons, therefore makes the original integral ambient exchange invertible.

proof.text:
For rational $\Lambda$, write $T_W=\Lambda_W\otimes^L_{A_W}-$ and take a generator $T_XJ$ of the integral-generation lemma. Step 1 gives $a^*J\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_C,A)$. The proper scalar-comparison lemma applies to $f,J$ and $f_C,a^*J$, giving invertible comparisons $\rho_f$ and $\rho_{f_C}$. The scalar/pullback comparisons $\lambda_u:u_\Lambda^*T\xrightarrow{\sim}T u_A^*$ are invertible and coherent. The two arrows from $c_\Lambda^*T_YRf_{*,A}J$ to $Rf_{C,*,\Lambda}T_{X_C}a_A^*J$ satisfy
$$Rf_{C,*,\Lambda}(\lambda_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{T_XJ}\circ c_\Lambda^*(\rho_f)
=\rho_{f_C}\circ T_C(\operatorname{Ex}^{A}_J)\circ\lambda_c.$$
Indeed apply the counit transpose for $f_C$ to each side. The pasted-mates counit formula cancels the units in the two coefficient projections and in exchange; both transposes are the pullback of $T_X(\varepsilon_{f,A,J})$, preceded by the same scalar/pullback composition comparison. Coherence of the scalar/pullback mate equates these preceding comparisons, and adjunction bijectivity gives the displayed equality. Step 3 makes $\operatorname{Ex}^{A}_J$ invertible; every comparison in the display is invertible. Hence the actual rational exchange is invertible on each $T_XJ$.

proof.text: For completeness, the actual exchange is a transformation of exact functors with their canonical shifts in this qcqs setting. Exact pullback is represented termwise, while the additive ordinary pushforward has the K-injective triangulated derived functor. The canonical exact-left/right-derived adjunction has shift-compatible unit and counit. The pullback square comparison is the localization of the degreewise inverse-image composition comparison: the exact-derived composition and natural-isomorphism factorizations show that on $M[n]$ it has the same components as on $M$ shifted by $n$; both differentials acquire $(-1)^n$. Its inverse has the same property. Whiskering and composing these shift-compatible unit, square and counit maps proves shift compatibility of the actual exchange. Thus its naturality squares also include the connecting arrow in every distinguished triangle.

source.place: Tags 015F and 0DVC: exact derived functors and the canonical derived adjunction; termwise check of square comparison

proof.text: Restrict the two rational exchange functors to $\mathcal L_X=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$. The proper localizing-coproduct theorem applies to $f$ with its given $S,q$; it applies to $f_C$ with base $C$ and $q=\mathrm{id}_C$. Pullback $a^*$ preserves the generating input classes by step 1 and is exact and preserves coproducts as a left adjoint, hence carries $\mathcal L_X$ into $\mathcal L_{X_C}$. The same adjoint argument for $c^*$ shows that both exchange functors preserve coproducts on $\mathcal L_X$. Step 5 and the localizing determination theorem therefore show that the isomorphism locus of the actual exchange on this domain is localizing. It contains $\mathcal G_X$ by step 4. The integral-generation lemma puts every rational $L\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$ in $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal G_X)\subseteq\mathcal L_X$, so exchange is invertible on $L$. Together with steps 1--3 this covers the full admissible coefficient list with the stated all-continuous norm-topological algebraic closure.
